text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

I'll ask a few questions before drafting, because this update has to do two hard things: get existing investors to put in more money, and tell them about a cheaper competitor. Below is how I'd build the argument from what you've given me. Correct anything that's wrong.

**How the argument fits together**

- **Claim:** Put money into the $600k bridge, because the company is on a path to profitability.
- **What you can show them:**
  - You've gone from 12 to 31 paying beekeepers in a year (2.6×).
  - Each sensor earns $17 over its cost, and each hive also pays $4 a month for the app.
  - Revenue for the half was $212k.
  - Your biggest customer's winter losses fell from 31% to 18%.
- **The link:** Growth in customers and recurring revenue at a positive margin leads to profit once you have enough hives.
- **The money:** $340k at $95k a month is about 3.6 months. Revenue outside the season looks like ~$16k a month, so you probably have until roughly March. That's the month your sales usually arrive (70% came in March–April). This is your strongest argument for the bridge: it gets you into the season that pays for the year. I'd lead with it.
- **What investors will push back on:**
  1. **The competitor.** A large company is selling at $45. That's $10 below your price and only $7 above your cost to make a sensor. Every investor will have seen it. The update has to answer it, not skip it.
  2. **The colony-loss result is mixed up.** Your customer also changed his mite treatment, so the fair claim is "he credits the sensors as part of it," not "the sensors cut his losses."
  3. **The profit claim.** See below.

**The profit claim needs your decision.** Right now you spend about $1.14M a year. If the second half brought in what the first did, you'd have about $424k in revenue, and only part of that is profit after the cost of the hardware. "Profitable next year" means more than doubling revenue, cutting spend sharply, or both. Nothing you've given me shows that yet. An investor who runs the numbers will spot the gap, and it would undermine the rest of the update. There are two ways to fix it:

- **(a)** You give me the plan and its numbers, and I write the claim plainly.
- **(b)** I write a narrower claim tied to something they can check, for example: "We reach monthly profitability by [month] if we have [X] hives on the app by [date]." It would also say what you'll do if you miss it.

Which do you want? Here's what I need either way:

1. **The profit plan.** How many hives are on the app right now, and what's your monthly recurring revenue? What hive or customer count, and what monthly spend, gets you to profit, and by when? Does "profitable" mean the full year or a monthly figure? Does the $95k a month include the cost of making sensors?
2. **Your answer to the $45 sensor.** What does yours do that theirs doesn't? Have you won or lost any customers since May? Can your $38 cost come down?
3. **The bridge terms.** What kind of deal is it (SAFE, note, or other), and at what cap or discount? When does it close, and what's the minimum cheque? Has anyone already committed? What do you plan to reach with it, and by when?
4. **Your biggest customer.** Can I name him or quote him? Do you have loss or churn numbers across your other customers?
5. **The reporting period.** Which six months does the $212k cover? I'm assuming January–June.
6. **Anything investors will find out anyway.** Is there a delay, a lost customer, a product problem, or a number that's weaker than it looks?

Once I have your answers, I'll write the update in under 600 words.

Go with (b). I can't promise profit next year, so use a claim the numbers support.

1. Don't know the hive count on the app or the monthly recurring revenue offhand. Not sure if the $95k includes making sensors. What I can commit to: bringing spend down to $75k a month by February by not filling two open roles.
2. Theirs only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. Haven't lost anyone, but three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor. Don't know if the $38 can come down.
3. Convertible note, 20% discount, $6M cap. Closes December 15. Investors who want in should reply to me by December 1. One angel has already committed $250k. Don't know a minimum cheque. I'll send a monthly cash report to everyone who puts money into the bridge.
4. Don't know if I can name or quote him. No numbers across the other customers.
5. Not sure of the exact months.
6. Just the three beekeepers testing the competitor's sensor.

I've written the update with the narrower claim. The bridge carries you through the 2027 pollination season on lower spend, and investors watch the numbers every month as they come in. You don't promise profit.

**Subject: Half-year update, and a bridge round I'd like you in**

Hi all,

In short: we've grown from 12 to 31 paying beekeepers in a year, a large competitor launched a cheaper sensor in May, and we're raising a $600,000 bridge to carry us through the 2027 pollination season on a lower cost base. I'm asking you to join it.

**Where we are**

- **31 paying commercial beekeepers**, up from 12 a year ago.
- **$212,000 in revenue** over the last six months. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season. Beekeepers buy before the season, so our revenue arrives in one large spring wave.
- **Every sale makes money.** A sensor costs us $38 to make and sells for $55. Each hive also pays $4 a month for the app.
- **Results in the field.** Our largest customer runs 4,000 hives. Over the winter he lost 18% of his colonies, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of that. He also changed his mite treatment, so we can't separate the two. We don't yet have loss figures across our other customers.

**The competitor**

In May a large farm equipment company launched a hive sensor at $45, $10 below our price. Their sensor measures temperature only. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. We haven't lost a customer to them. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor, and I'd rather tell you that now than have you hear it later. Those three trials will be the first real test of whether the extra measurements are worth $10 to a commercial beekeeper.

**Cash**

We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left. At that rate the money runs out around March, just as the season's revenue starts to arrive. That timing is why we're raising now.

We're bringing spend down to $75,000 a month by February by not filling two open roles.

With the bridge and the lower spend, we have cash into late 2027 before counting any revenue. That covers the whole of next season.

**What I am and am not promising**

I'm not going to tell you we'll be profitable next year. I can't yet back that with numbers. What I can tell you is what the bridge buys: one full season at $75,000 a month, which will show whether our customer growth and app revenue can pay for this business. You won't have to wait until the end of it to find out. Everyone who puts money into the bridge gets a monthly cash report from me.

**The bridge**

- $600,000 convertible note, 20% discount, $6M cap.
- One angel has already committed $250,000, so $350,000 remains.
- The round closes December 15. **If you want in, please reply to me by December 1.**

If we don't raise it, we reach March with almost no cash, just before the months that bring in most of our revenue. With it, we go into the season fully funded, running leaner, and with you seeing every month's numbers.

You backed us when we had 12 beekeepers. I'd like you with us for the season that tells us what this company can be. Reply by December 1, or just hit reply with questions.

Thanks,
</final_document>

Before you send it:

- **Sign it.** I left the signature line empty because I don't know how you sign these.
- **Things I left out because you didn't know them:** your biggest customer's name and a quote from him, the reporting months, a minimum cheque, and whether the $38 cost can come down. The piece works without them. If he agrees to be named or quoted, that paragraph gets stronger.
- **Investors will ask what profit would take.** At $75k a month, the business needs about $900k a year in gross profit to cover its costs. Revenue was $212k for the half. I didn't put a break-even figure in the update because it depends on two things you don't know yet: whether the $95k includes making sensors, and how many hives are paying for the app. Once you have both, a line like "we break even at X hives on the app" would make your best argument for the round.
- **Runway check:** about 2.5 months at $95k, then $75k a month from February, on $940k (the $340k you have plus the $600k bridge). That lasts to around November 2027 before any revenue. Please check it against your actual bank balance.
